newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent differentials fade in Chicago.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent differentials fade in Chicago.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel differentials eased in Chicago on Friday in the wake of rising front-month futures prices, traders said.
The weakening differentials ended a steady run-up in spot prices in the Chicago and Group Three markets fueled by surging NYMEX heating oil and unleaded prices.
Front-month heating oil rose more than 3.0 cents a gallon and the sister unleaded contract was up more than 2.0 cents a gallon in the NYMEX floor session on Friday.
"Chicago tanked," one trader said of the expected turndown in spot-market differentials.
Traders had expected prices to ease on perceptions of ample stocks in the region, but said some buyers were drawn into the spot markets late this week after prices eased on a midweek NYMEX sell-off.
"I think there's been some bottom picking," one Group Three trader said of buying interest holding differentials steady in the face of higher futures prices over the past two days.
High sulphur diesel eased to bids 7.50 cents a gallon under the print in Chicago and was talked 6.75/7.25 cents under in Group Three.
Chicago unleaded gasoline differentials dropped to bids 5.25 cents a gallon under the print for prompt deliveries and 4.50 cents under for later deliveries.
Group Three unleaded eased to 4.75/4.50 cents a gallon under the print for prompt deliveries and 5.0/4.75 cents under for later deliveries.
